Rule 30 keeps a pronominal suffix out of the fusion of a preposition with its construct noun: it takes whatever English pronoun the ASV writes for it under rule 18. The one pronoun of 'turning it' denotes the dish, exactly as this 3fs suffix does, and rule 30 reserves 'added' for English no morpheme licenses. Marking the suffix unrepresented and the pronoun added, on the parallel of 'wiping it' where no pronominal morpheme stands in the clause, was the competing reading.

'upon ... face' is recast as the single adverbial expression 'upside down'; no English word is spent on the preposition apart from the noun or on the noun apart from the preposition, so the two contiguous morphemes share one unit under rule 30, headed on the noun carrying the lexeme.

review_notes: Corrected the flagged three-morpheme unit: rule 30 states that a pronominal suffix on the construct noun is no part of such a fusion, so 'upside down' is the preposition and noun only, and the suffix takes the written 'it' under rule 18.

The 'it' of 'wiping it' remains added, since that clause writes no pronominal morpheme; the two supplied-looking pronouns are treated differently because the Hebrew clauses differ, not because of English parallelism.
